Sub-theme 'Grid-connected PV: performance and techno-economics in buildings, campuses and utility plants' of group 1: 8 studies, cite as \cite{R0034,R0054,R0095,R0335,R0348,R0409,R0452,R1780}. Methods: techno-economic assessment 6; empirical case study 2. Settings: sectors: buildings-residential 5; multi-sector 1; buildings-commercial-institutional 1; transport 1 | departments: Bogotá D.C. 5; Atlántico 3; Valle del Cauca 2; Antioquia 2; La Guajira 1; none stated 1. Technical outcomes: campus performance ratio 0.73-0.78 [R0335]; PVsyst performance ratio 84.2% [R0095]; north campus carport supplied 1.7% of campus demand [R0335]. Economic outcomes: IRR 20.74% in Barranquilla (3.5 kWp) and 16.22% in Bogota [R0034]; IRR 9.1%, payback 8.5 years (Medellin) [R0452]; payback 10.2 (levels 1-2) to 6.0 years (Bogota) [R0409]; IRR 11.05% and 13-year payback for a yard-based bus-fleet PV plant [R1780]; storage only profitable with price drops (11.26% IRR at 25% lower storage price) [R0034]. Environmental outcomes: avoided CO2 about 20.4 t in 25 years [R0095]; 346 kg CO2 avoided per 2 kW system [R0409]; about 193 kgCO2/yr saved per household [R0452]; avoided CO2 by 2050 Bogota 7,106.51 t [R0348]. Pattern: Techno-economic assessments report IRR and payback that vary widely by city and system size (IRR 9.1% in Medellin [R0452] to 20.74% in Barranquilla [R0034]; payback 10.2 (levels 1-2) to 6.0 years (Bogota) in R0409), and performance ratios (0.73-0.78 in R0335; 84.2% in R0095) are reported on different bases; R0034 finds storage profitable only with price drops. Avoided-CO2 figures use different units and horizons (R0095, R0409, R0452, R0348) and are not directly comparable. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Solar policy, diffusion and power-system integration' of group 1: 9 studies, cite as \cite{R0104,R0115,R0200,R0230,R0382,R0400,R0464,R0505,R0517}. Methods: modelling/simulation 7; literature review 2. Settings: sectors: buildings-residential 5; power-generation-SIN 2; multi-sector 2 | departments: Antioquia 2; Chocó 1; none stated 7. Technical outcomes: rooftop PV 4,400-10,600 MW by 2035 [R0104]; about 7532 MW PV by 2040 under FIT and subsidy, 7029 MW under net metering [R0115]; 1, 2 and 3 kW households give 2.5, 11 and 16 GW PV by 2035 [R0382]; PV adoption converges to 25-30% of households [R0200]; about 6 million adopter households by 2027 [R0517]; 5.82 MW by 2035 under the aggressive scheme [R0505]; about 5.28 MW PV installed [R0464]. Economic outcomes: net metering most efficient (20,298 USD/MW), capital subsidy least efficient (509,616 USD/MW) [R0115]; household tariff rises 0.13 to 0.20 USD/kWh [R0104]; tariffs for non-PV households rise about 20% by 2040 [R0200]; grid tariffs rise to 0.37 USD/kWh [R0517]; at 3 kW utilities recover 0% of costs, and net billing restores 100% cost recovery [R0382]; minimum FiT to start diffusion USD 0.30/kWh [R0505]; urban EMS daily savings USD 2711.57 (27.30%) [R0400]. Environmental outcomes: urban 3472.28 kg CO2 (27.69%) and rural 6019.45 kg CO2 (35.38%) daily reductions with EMS [R0400]. Pattern: Simulation studies agree that adoption scenarios raise grid tariffs for non-PV households (R0104, R0200, R0517), and that the support scheme matters (net metering most efficient at 20,298 USD/MW in R0115; at 3 kW utilities recover 0% of costs in R0382), but projected PV capacity ranges from 5.28 MW installed (R0464) to 2.5, 11 and 16 GW by 2035 (R0382) because scope and units differ; R0400 is an energy-management study with its own daily savings metrics. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Off-grid, solar-thermal and productive-use solar applications' of group 1: 7 studies, cite as \cite{R0116,R0245,R0332,R0333,R0387,R0451,R0623}. Methods: modelling/simulation 3; techno-economic assessment 2; qualitative social study 1; policy analysis 1. Settings: sectors: non-interconnected-zones 2; buildings-residential 2; multi-sector 2; power-generation-SIN 1 | departments: Chocó 1; Valle del Cauca 1; Santander 1; La Guajira 1; Antioquia 1; Atlántico 1; Norte de Santander 1; Bolívar 1; none stated 1. Technical outcomes: direct-expansion solar heat pump annual COP about 3.5, solar fraction above 88% [R0451]; hybrid solar gas-turbine efficiency 35% without solar input falling to 30% at midday [R0623]; solar RO desalination pumping energy 5.91 kWh/m3 [R0333]. Economic outcomes: LCOH below 0.075 USD/kWh [R0451]; IRR 2% and payback 4 years for a portable solar water machine [R0116]; STESS capex USD 22,711, about 30 times the USD 738 of conventional heaters [R0332]; diesel electricity costs USD 0.26/kWh [R0245]. Environmental outcomes: about 916.2 kg CO2/year avoided per house [R0245]. Pattern: Outcomes are heterogeneous: COP and solar fraction for a solar heat pump (R0451), turbine efficiency (R0623), desalination pumping energy (R0333), IRR and payback for a portable solar water machine (R0116), and capex of a solar thermal storage heater against conventional heaters (R0332). Costs are given against different references (LCOH in R0451, diesel electricity cost in R0245, conventional heaters in R0332), and only R0245 quantifies avoided CO2 (about 916.2 kg CO2/year per house); values are not directly comparable. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Wind power: onshore, small and offshore (resource, siting, grid integration, economics, barriers)' of group 1: 7 studies, cite as \cite{R0083,R0127,R0336,R0367,R0378,R0384,R0445}. Methods: modelling/simulation 4; empirical case study 1; literature review 1; qualitative social study 1. Settings: sectors: power-generation-SIN 6; non-interconnected-zones 1 | departments: Bolívar 2; La Guajira 2; Atlántico 2; Magdalena 1; Boyacá 1; Cundinamarca 1; Cauca 1; Nariño 1; none stated 3. Technical outcomes: capacity factors 1.2-34.2% after losses across five sites [R0445]; wind capacity only 19.5 MW [R0378]; VAWT Cp 0.15-0.35 [R0127]; 28,849 MW wind by 2050 in Green Democracy [R0083]; La Guajira 482 W/m2 (110.8 m) and Barranquilla 857 W/m2 [R0367]; lowest wind speed 2.403 m/s [R0336]. Economic outcomes: wind share 31.0% in the minimum-volatility portfolio [R0384]. Environmental outcomes: avoided emissions 1.2 Mt (vs hydro) and 149.7 Mt CO2e (vs coal) [R0083]; Villa Teresa 34.16% CF but exclusionary environmental limits [R0445]. Pattern: Resource and capacity-factor results span a wide range between sites (capacity factors 1.2-34.2% after losses across five sites in R0445; La Guajira 482 W/m2 (110.8 m) and Barranquilla 857 W/m2 in R0367; lowest wind speed 2.403 m/s in R0336), while installed wind capacity is only 19.5 MW (R0378). R0083 and R0384 are scenario and portfolio studies (28,849 MW wind by 2050 in R0083; wind share 31.0% in the minimum-volatility portfolio of R0384), and R0127 reports VAWT Cp 0.15-0.35; environmental evidence is limited to R0083 and R0445. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Hydropower, hydrokinetic, geothermal and ocean energy' of group 1: 7 studies, cite as \cite{R0167,R0190,R0296,R0424,R0475,R0544,R1450}. Methods: empirical case study 3; qualitative social study 2; modelling/simulation 1; literature review 1. Settings: sectors: power-generation-SIN 5; non-interconnected-zones 1; industry 1 | departments: Chocó 1; Boyacá 1; none stated 5. Technical outcomes: Savonius turbine 1 m2 gives ~142 W and 1245 kWh/y [R0424]; rewinding raised minimum breakdown voltage from 38.4 to 95.6 kV [R0475]; dry climate cuts hydropower about 10% by 2050 [R0167]; geothermal pilot peaked at 77 kWe [R1450]; salinity gradient technical potential 780 MW [R0190]. Economic outcomes: winding failure would cost 14-28 million USD vs ~1.7 million USD for rewinding [R0475]; GDP growth reduced up to 0.28% by dry climate [R0167]. Environmental outcomes: about 23,675 people displaced by about 30% of installed capacity [R0544]; emissions cut about 94% versus oil generation [R0424]; geothermal carbon footprint cut 19% (OFA) and 11% (OFB) [R1450]; acceptance of geothermal electricity 84.72% [R0296]. Pattern: Evidence comes from single-technology studies with no shared metric: climate impact on hydropower (about 10% cut by 2050 and GDP growth reduced up to 0.28% in R0167), a hydrokinetic Savonius turbine (~142 W and 1245 kWh/y in R0424), generator rewinding (R0475), a geothermal pilot (peak 77 kWe; carbon footprint cut 19% and 11% in R1450) and salinity-gradient potential (780 MW in R0190). Social outcomes come from R0544 (about 23,675 people displaced) and R0296 (acceptance of geothermal electricity 84.72%); there is no cross-study replication. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Biogas, anaerobic digestion and municipal-waste-to-energy (incl. incentive effects)' of group 2: 8 studies, cite as \cite{R0051,R0154,R0206,R0218,R0286,R0435,R0446,R0495}. Methods: Study types: review 3; other 2; techno-economic-assessment 2; empirical-case-study 1. Aspen Plus or cost-based TEA in R0446; literature reviews in R0154, R0206, R0286; Techno-economic models with IRR/NPV/LCOE (R0495); multi-criteria ranking (R0051).. Settings: Sectors: agriculture 4; multi-sector 3; buildings-residential 1. Departments: Santander 1; Antioquia 1; Córdoba 1; Atlántico 1; 4 studies national or unspecified.. Technical outcomes: BMP 0.03-0.78 Nm3 CH4/kg VS [R0154]; AcoD raised yield 14-22% [R0154]; average biogas 2.6 m3/d, 0.21 m3 biogas/kg biomass [R0218]; Theoretical biogas potential 149,436 TJ/year and technical potential 53,554 TJ/year [R0286]; 996 digesters, 79% tubular psychrophilic [R0154]; only about 30% of large-scale biogas used [R0154]; HCCI engine net indicated efficiency about 32%, intake temperature above 320 C [R0435]; Energy potential 1,001-3,283 MWh/day [R0495]; TOPSIS ranking: anaerobic digestion 78.2%, gasification 47.5%, incineration 27.4%, landfill gas 6.6% [R0051]. Economic outcomes: 7 m3 biodigester yields about US$400/year fuel savings [R0206]; Polyethylene digesters cheapest: 18.2 M USD for 150,718 households [R0446]; LPG saving USD 30/month [R0218]; incineration NPV 396-412 million USD [R0495]; landfill gate fee 7.8 USD/t [R0495]. Environmental outcomes: biogas cuts firewood GHG to 11% [R0446]; avoiding 0.52 t CO2eq/month [R0218]; low-cost digesters cut impacts up to 80% [R0154]; GHG 46-92% below landfilling [R0495]; GHG mitigated weighted 16.17% [R0051]. Pattern: Biogas studies report outcomes on different bases (BMP 0.03-0.78 Nm3 CH4/kg VS and AcoD yield gains of 14-22% in R0154; 0.21 m3 biogas/kg biomass in R0218; theoretical biogas potential 149,436 TJ/year versus technical potential 53,554 TJ/year in R0286). Household digester economics are favourable (about US$400/year fuel savings in R0206; LPG saving USD 30/month in R0218) and GHG reductions are reported in R0446, R0218, R0154 and R0495 (46-92% below landfilling in R0495). For waste-to-energy, R0051 ranks anaerobic digestion first by TOPSIS (78.2%) ahead of gasification, incineration and landfill gas, while R0495 reports incineration NPV of 396-412 million USD. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Biomass resource potential, bioenergy systems, scenarios, policy and sustainability frameworks' of group 2: 7 studies, cite as \cite{R0094,R0114,R0152,R0323,R0338,R0374,R0520}. Methods: Study types: modelling-simulation 3; other 2; review 1; empirical-case-study 1. Residue-to-product-ratio inventories with energy equations (R0323, R0338); Scenario or energy-system models (LEAP in R0152, R0520; TIMES in R0374); sustainability indicator model (R0094); reviews and legal analysis (R0114).. Settings: Sectors: multi-sector 6; agriculture 1. Departments: Santander 1; Norte de Santander 1; 6 studies national or unspecified.. Technical outcomes: Silos highest TEP (up to 208 TJ/yr) [R0323]; source choice changed TEP by up to 30% [R0323]; Residues total 185.66 million t/yr [R0338]; bagasse gives 99.12% of biomass electricity [R0338]; Biomass supplies 315-760 PJ/y of modern bio-based products by 2050 [R0374]; fossil share falls from 76% to 35-39% [R0374]; theoretical bioenergy potential 550,000 TJ vs technical 35,000 TJ (6%) [R0114]; biofuel imports up to 76% [R0152, R0520]. Economic outcomes: Mobilising biomass cuts system cost by up to 11 billion USD/y and marginal abatement cost by 62% [R0374]. Environmental outcomes: bioenergy scenarios cut 11.4, 20.3, 22.6, 24.4 MtCO2-eq by 2030 (5-11%) [R0152]; cuts 2030 GHG emissions by 11.4-22.6 MtCO2-eq (5-10% vs baseline 223 MtCO2-eq) [R0520]; BECCS gives 24-29% of cumulative avoided emissions [R0374]. Pattern: Potential estimates depend on method and scope: theoretical bioenergy potential 550,000 TJ versus technical 35,000 TJ (6%) in R0114; residues total 185.66 million t/yr with bagasse giving 99.12% of biomass electricity in R0338; source choice changed TEP by up to 30% in R0323. Scenario models (LEAP in R0152 and R0520; TIMES in R0374) all find that bioenergy lowers emissions (11.4-22.6 MtCO2-eq by 2030 in R0520, similar in R0152; BECCS gives 24-29% of cumulative avoided emissions in R0374) but use different baselines; R0094 is a sustainability indicator model. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Liquid biofuels, microalgae and biorefineries' of group 2: 5 studies, cite as \cite{R0012,R0185,R0211,R0272,R0519}. Methods: Study types: modelling-simulation 3; review 1; empirical-case-study 1. LCA (R0012, R0211, R0519); supply-chain optimisation (R0185); reviews (R0272).. Settings: Sectors: industry 2; transport 1; agriculture 1; multi-sector 1. Departments: Cesar 1; Atlántico 1; La Guajira 1; Meta 1; Bolívar 1; Cauca 1; 1 studies national or unspecified.. Technical outcomes: Energy balance -1809 (CS), 90 (CS+AD), -82 (DS), 637 TJ/yr (DS+AD) [R0211]; 12 biodiesel plants, 7 bioethanol plants [R0272]; microalgae need at least 52% less land than oil palm and 67% less than sugarcane [R0185]. Economic outcomes: not reported. Environmental outcomes: GWP ranged from -287.37 g CO2-eq/FU to 10.219 [R0012]; 8 of 11 cases net negative via land use change [R0012]; GHG 5.3, 0.4, 1.4, -0.3 kgCO2eq/L EtOH [R0211]; GHG 149 (VLT), 93 (ST1), 105 (ST2) kg CO2 eq/t starch [R0519]; biogas cut VLT emissions 72% [R0519]; <5.3% of microalgal areas overlap rainforest vs 30.5-32.4% for oil palm and sugarcane [R0185]. Pattern: Evidence is dominated by life-cycle assessment, and GWP varies strongly with feedstock and land-use change (-287.37 g CO2-eq/FU to 10.219 in R0012, with 8 of 11 cases net negative via land use change; GHG 5.3, 0.4, 1.4 and -0.3 kgCO2eq/L EtOH in R0211; GHG 149, 93 and 105 kg CO2 eq/t starch in R0519). Functional units differ, so values are not directly comparable; R0185 adds land-use evidence for microalgae, R0272 an inventory of plants, and no economic outcomes are reported. (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)

Sub-theme 'Hybrid microgrid sizing, operation and techno-economics (off-grid zones and grid-connected)' of group 3: 13 studies, cite as \cite{R0002,R0010,R0042,R0100,R0228,R0418,R0430,R0645,R0668,R0848,R0855,R1456,R1558}. Methods: Study types: modelling-simulation 11; techno-economic-assessment 2. Method keywords (matched in the extracted method field): genetic algorithm 4; PSO 3; HOMER 2; iHOGA 2; MILP/MINLP/NLP/LP 2; optimal power flow/dispatch/unit commitment 2; review/bibliometric 1. Settings: Sectors: non-interconnected-zones 13. Departments/scope: La Guajira 7; Chocó 4; Amazonas 2; San Andrés y Providencia 2; Boyacá 1; Arauca 1; Valle del Cauca 1; Nariño 1; Guaviare 1; Guainía 1; national scope 1. Technical outcomes: PV-battery optimum with diesel never selected: PV 22-29 kWp plus battery 74-93 kWh [R0010] | 100% renewable share with zero diesel fuel use [R0042]; 96.81% renewable share [R0002] | LPSP under 0.25% in diesel-assisted configurations [R0418] | simplified battery models overestimate life up to three times [R0002]. Economic outcomes: LCOE 0.35-0.38 US$/kWh vs 0.86-4.51 US$/kWh for diesel [R0010] | LCOE 0.49 EUR/kWh for current system, 0.36 EUR/kWh optimal lead-acid, 0.20 EUR/kWh lithium option [R0002] | LCOE 0.23-0.35 USD/kWh diesel-assisted vs 0.29-0.44 USD/kWh fully renewable [R0418] | lowest LCOE 0.161 USD/kWh with PV, 0.524 USD/kWh for Case I [R1558] | LCOE 0.754 USD/kWh (environmental priority) vs 0.514 USD/kWh (economic priority) [R0668]; 1,087.69 (Chocó), 857.15 (La Guajira) and 867.42 (Guainía) COP/kWh [R0855] | LCOE 1.61 $/Wh (SHS 1) down to 0.65 $/Wh (GF/SHS 3) [R0228] | payback 2.01 years [R0042]; 25-year expenses 88.4% lower than diesel-only [R0042] | dispatch cost 189, 182 and 196 COP/kWh vs 518 COP/kWh for the traditional grid [R0645]. Environmental outcomes: no-diesel variant about 60% lower emissions [R0418] | avoids 4248 kt CO2/yr versus grid [R0100] | 18.97 tCO2e/yr vs 29.94 tCO2e/yr across objective priorities [R0668]. Pattern: Studies agree that PV/wind-battery hybrids undercut diesel (LCOE 0.35-0.38 US$/kWh versus 0.86-4.51 US$/kWh for diesel in R0010; 25-year expenses 88.4% lower than diesel-only in R0042; dispatch cost 189, 182 and 196 COP/kWh versus 518 COP/kWh for the traditional grid in R0645), but cost metrics differ in currency and unit (US$, EUR, USD, COP/kWh and $/Wh in R0228), so figures are not directly comparable. Fully renewable designs cost more than diesel-assisted ones (LCOE 0.29-0.44 versus 0.23-0.35 USD/kWh in R0418) while cutting emissions (no-diesel variant about 60% lower), and battery model choice matters (simplified models overestimate life up to three times in R0002). (Values are the extracted values; each bracketed record id is the study reporting that value and is cited as \cite{<id>}.)
